title: Localization orthogonality for derived internal Hom
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $f$ be a global section. Write $\mathcal O_f$ for the sheafified sectionwise localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization, def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-section-localization], with its canonical ring map $\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_f$, and use the unbounded derived categories of $\mathcal O$-modules and $\mathcal O_f$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ and $L\in D(\mathcal O_f)$, viewed as an $\mathcal O$-complex by restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], there is a natural isomorphism $$R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,K)\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_f}(L,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal O_f,K)).$$ Consequently, if $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal O_f,K)=0$, then $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,K)=0$ for every $L\in D(\mathcal O_f)$. No boundedness, finite-generation, or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0996, lemma-map-twice-localize, clause (2), and Tag 0997, lemma-hom-from-Af, implication (1) => (2).

proof.text: Put $S=\mathcal O_f$ and let $U:\operatorname{Mod}(S)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ be restriction of scalars. It leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged. The kernel and cokernel descriptions in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] therefore give $U(\ker a)=\ker U(a)$ and $U(\operatorname{coker}a)=\operatorname{coker}U(a)$: sectionwise kernels are unchanged, and the underlying sheafification of the sectionwise additive quotient is unchanged. Thus $U$ is additive and exact, and it detects zero objects and acyclic complexes. In particular termwise restriction sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and gives the restriction functor on the derived categories.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian, and Section 03D9, section-kernels; elementary exactness of restriction of scalars

proof.text: For an $\mathcal O$-module $N$, set $H(N)=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(S,N)$ with $S$-action $(b\phi)_W(c)=\phi_W(b|_Wc)$ for $W\to V$, $b\in S(V)$ and $c\in S(W)$. The sheaf Hom definition gives a sheaf; associativity and the unit law follow from those of multiplication in $S$, and postcomposition defines the additive functor $H$. For an $S$-module $M$, an $\mathcal O$-linear map $a:UM\to N$ gives an $S$-linear map $\widetilde a:M\to H(N)$ by $\widetilde a_V(m)_W(c)=a_W(c\,m|_W)$. Conversely $b:M\to H(N)$ gives $m\mapsto b_V(m)_V(1)$. These are inverse: evaluation recovers $a(m)$, while $S$-linearity gives $b_W(c m|_W)_W(1)=b_V(m)_W(c)$. Both formulas commute with restriction and with pre- and postcomposition. Hence $U\dashv H$. This explicitly proves the elementary adjunction of Tag 0932; no adjunction for ordinary modules is silently applied to sheaves.

Choose a complex $F^\bullet$ of $S$-modules representing $L$, and a K-injective resolution $K^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ over $\mathcal O$, using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Its small-site hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis on $\mathcal C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(S)$, $v=U$ and $u=H$. Both categories are abelian, $U$ is exact by step 1, and step 2 gives the additive adjunction. Thus $H(I^\bullet)$ is K-injective as an $S$-complex. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], its underlying $\mathcal O$-complex represents $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(S,K)$, since $S$ is placed in degree zero. This supplies the $S$-module structure required in the inner argument on the right of the claimed isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0996, lemma-map-twice-localize, proof of (2); generic preservation is Stacks 08BJ

proof.text: Apply the two formulas of step 2 on every slice $\mathcal C/V$ to each pair $(F^p,I^{p+n})$. They give mutually inverse sheaf maps between $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(UF^p,I^{p+n})$ and $\mathcal Hom_S(F^p,H(I^{p+n}))$. Taking their product over $p\in\mathbf Z$ gives an isomorphism $\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{\mathcal O}(UF^\bullet,I^\bullet)\cong U\mathcal Hom^\bullet_S(F^\bullet,H(I^\bullet))$. Explicitly the degree-$n$ map sends $(a^p)_p$ to $(m\mapsto(c\mapsto a^p(cm)))_p$, with inverse evaluation at $1$. It commutes with the differential: $d_Ia^p-(-1)^na^{p+1}d_F$ is sent to $H(d_I)\widetilde a^p-(-1)^n\widetilde a^{p+1}d_F$, since $d_F(cm)=c\,d_F(m)$. The formulas commute with all restriction maps, so they prove an isomorphism of sheaf complexes, not just of global Hom groups.

source.place: Tag 0996, proof of (2), final displayed equality; degreewise form of Tag 0932

proof.text: The two complexes in step 4 compute the two derived internal Homs by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]: $I^\bullet$ is K-injective over $\mathcal O$, and $H(I^\bullet)$ is K-injective over $S$ by step 3. Localizing the isomorphism therefore proves the claimed isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O)$, with the right side restricted from $D(S)$. It is natural: step 4 commutes with maps of $F^\bullet$ and $I^\bullet$ by its formulas. The representative comparisons and functoriality of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] descend this naturality in $F^\bullet$ through quasi-isomorphisms. For the second argument, every derived morphism between K-injective representatives is represented by a chain map modulo homotopy by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Additivity of $H$ and the Hom-complex formulas preserve these homotopies. Thus the same naturality holds for all morphisms of $K$ and is independent of the chosen representatives.

Suppose $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(S,K)=0$. Then every cohomology sheaf of $UH(I^\bullet)$ is zero, because cohomology factors through the derived category. Exactness and detection of zero by $U$ from step 1 imply that $H(I^\bullet)$ is acyclic as an $S$-complex. Thus the quasi-isomorphism $0\to H(I^\bullet)$ identifies it with zero in $D(S)$. The zero complex is K-injective (every map into it is zero), so derived internal Hom from $L$ into this zero object can be computed as $\mathcal Hom^\bullet_S(F^\bullet,0)=0$. Step 5 now gives $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,K)=0$. All products above are the products in the Hom-complex definition; the argument imposes no bound on $F^\bullet$ or $I^\bullet$, and uses neither finite generation nor flatness.

The statement matches 0996(2) and 0997 (1)=>(2) hypothesis by hypothesis: a commutative sheaf of rings on a site small in the module universe, the isomorphism in D(O) with the right side restricted from D(O_f), and no change of coefficient category. Step 1: restriction U is exact and detects acyclicity, since kernels and sheafified cokernels are unchanged. Step 2: I checked the adjunction U -| Hom_O(O_f,-) and its inverse formulas, including O- and O_f-linearity; it uses commutativity, which holds. Step 3: 08BJ is applied with u=H right adjoint to the exact v=U, the correct direction, and the degree-0 Hom complex gives RHom_O(O_f,K). Step 4: the differential sign identity and O-linearity of the slice-wise map hold. Step 5: naturality goes through 070I (a Mathlib leaf). Step 6: H(I) is acyclic, hence zero in D(O_f), so the right side vanishes. Small cases checked: f=1, f nilpotent, K=0 or L=0, the empty site, and Z with p (Hom and Ext^1 of Q into Z_p vanish). The delivery has no new nodes, and no existing node duplicates it; nearest candidates are rhom-calculus, local-hom-tower-criterion, module-localization-tower-vanishing and sc-sheaf-coinduction-adjunction (schemes only). I accept the declared tool_uses: lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective is a generic 08BJ tool, and prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist is already on the route through sk-def-sf-operations.
